analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (FlintPolicyTests.swift and FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests.swift); no production source, protocol, key-handling, attestation or cache code is modified, so no runtime security behavior changes.

FlintPolicyTests.swift (head lines ~130-146): the Flint KV quantization test is refined. A provider-wide global default of balanced/k8v8/k8v4 must resolve to .native for Flint, while per-model overrides (byModel) and the purpose-specific environment variable must throw flintRequiresNative. This only asserts the existing policy and does not weaken it. It touches TB-007 (inference engine) correctness and T-041 only indirectly: Flint uses native KV, with no new at-rest cache artifact. The production resolver `EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve(global:)` is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not confirm the actual production behavior behind the new assertion. This is a test-contract question for integration, not a vulnerability.

FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests.swift (head lines 37-39): the live test now uses default BackendSettings instead of explicitly forcing paged/native. It is opt-in via DARKBLOOM_FLINT_OPENROUTER_LIVE, uses attestationSigner nil, a localhost unused coordinator URL, and a test-tenant cache scope. It also still requires bridge.kvBackendKind == .paged at line 58, so it now validates production defaults. Test hygiene is unchanged: cache dir 0700, temp state root removed. The receipt file writes model content only in an opt-in test environment.

No new attack surface or regression against T-008, T-041, A-001 or the TB-002 trust assumptions was identified. Remaining uncertainty is limited to whether production defaults actually resolve as the tests assert, which would be covered by the test run rather than a security review.
